overview.description: Primers are short (~15-30 bp) sequences that kickstart PCR. The biggest challenge is designing them to prefer your template over each other - primer dimers can ruin a month. Aim for Tm 50-60C, GC 40-60%, and keep paired Tms within 5C.
objectives: apply length, GC%, Tm and GC-clamp guidelines
use Benchling/Primer3 and the NEB Tm Calculator

steps.description: Primers are short (~15-30 bp) sequences that kickstart PCR. The biggest challenge is designing them to prefer your template over each other - primer dimers can ruin a month. Aim for Tm 50-60C, GC 40-60%, and keep paired Tms within 5C.
steps.intro: Primers are short (~15-30 bp) sequences that kickstart PCR. The biggest challenge is designing them to prefer your template over each other - primer dimers can ruin a month. Aim for Tm 50-60C, GC 40-60%, and keep paired Tms within 5C.

instructions.title: Set parameters
instructions.description: Target length ~18-25 nt, GC 40-60%, Tm 50-60C, with a 3' GC clamp where possible.

instructions.title: Check for dimers
instructions.description: Use a design wizard to flag self-dimers, hairpins and primer-primer complementarity.

instructions.title: Validate specificity
instructions.description: BLAST your primers against the genome to rule out off-target binding.

instructions.title: Confirm Tm
instructions.description: Calculate annealing temperature with the NEB Tm Calculator for your specific polymerase.

submission.description: Design a validated primer pair, report Tm/GC/length for each, and show the dimer/specificity checks.
